references.text: The immediate context: Sarai had an Egyptian slave named Hagar, and she had not borne children to Abram.
Abram went to the land of Canaan, which is the starting point for the time reference 'ten years in the land of Canaan'.
The consequences of Sarah giving Hagar to Abram: conflict between Ishmael and Isaac, which led to Hagar and Ishmael being sent away.
A parallel practice: Rachel gave her slave Bilhah to Jacob as a wife to bear children through her.
Another parallel: Leah gave her slave Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.
Paul uses the story of Sarah and Hagar as an allegory for the two covenants—the son of the slave was born according to the flesh, while the son of the free woman was born through promise.
25:12 confirms and summarizes the consequence of the event in 16:3 by identifying Ishmael's origin.
Direct narrative connection: 16:15 is the direct result of the action in 16:3.
